page.name: Manual sending from the console
page.h1: Send and check messages from the console
page.metaTitle: Console manual send and message lookup
page.metaDescription: The console is where you send a message by hand, look up what happened to one, and read the logs behind a support question.
page.lede: Not every message comes from an API. Testing a new sender, resending after a fix, or simply looking up what a customer received — those are console jobs, and they should not require writing code.

bullets: Sending a message by hand, for a test or a one-off
Looking up a single message and reading its status and receipt
Filtering the logs behind a support question

p: Messages your application generates belong in your application, where they are reviewed, versioned and reproducible. The console is for the work that has no home in code: verifying a new sender, resending after a fix, reading the record when a customer asks what they received.

A message sent by hand goes out under the same channel, connection, pacing and suppression rules as one sent by API. There is no bypass, which is deliberate — a test send tells you what production will do.

faq.q: Do I need to log in to send?
faq.a: The console is behind authentication, and the send path itself sits under the same tenant as your API traffic.

faq.q: Can I use the console to send to a whole list?
faq.a: Bulk and scheduled sending exist as console features; their behavior is documented in the help center rather than summarized here.
The getting-started article walks from creating a connection to sending the first message, and the API keys article covers using the same tenant from code.
